Thanks again for taking the call today, Olivia  great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can keep momentum: 

Summary of today's call:
- Goal: migrate Acme's semantic search and recommendations from current vector provider to Redwood while keeping relevance at parity or better.
- Current infra: single-region vector DB (Pinecone), ~12M vectors, embedding model: "openai-text-embedding-ada-002" (1536 dims), real-time writes + nightly batch updates.

Proposed plan / asks:
1) SDK setup & auth (Marissa / Marcus)
   - We'll send a short integration guide and an API key scope for ingestion-only access. Marcus will own the workshop.
2) Embedding dims & normalization
   - Based on your current model (1536 dims) we recommend keeping 1536 for parity.
   - Normalize vectors to unit length (L2) if you plan to use cosine similarity; Redwood supports both dot-product and cosine in the reranker.
3) Batching strategy
   - Use the bulk ingestion endpoint with batches of 256-512 for backfills (tunable). For real-time writes use 1-32 per request to keep latency low.
4) Migration approach
   - Zero-downtime pattern: dual-write (write to Redwood + current provider) for 48-72 hours, backfill historical vectors in parallel, run A/B compare on a sample set, then cutover. See attached checklist.
5) Reranker & structured output
   - We can route candidate retrieval to your existing vector store and then run a lightweight reranker on Redwood to improve ordering. For structured output/tool-calling use our "structured-scorer" option to return JSON annotations.

Deliverables from Redwood by EOD Wed:
- Migration checklist (attached)
- HubSpot deal record with proposed SOW & timeline
- Proposed schedule for a 90-min technical workshop (Marcus + 2 engineers)

Can you confirm: (a) you can share a ~10k sample export CSV of id + vector (we can accept compressed CSV), (b) preferred window for the workshop (Tue/Wed next week)?

Hi Olivia  Marcus here (solutions engineering). Short answers + specifics below.

Normalization impact:
- If you're currently relying on Pinecone's internal cosine handling without normalizing on write, you may see small rank differences when we normalize on write because normalization changes vector magnitudes (but not direction). To keep apples-to-apples during A/B:
  - Option A: Don't normalize on write to Redwood and compute cosine at query time. Redwood supports cosine lookup without normalized vectors (we'll compute norms at query).
  - Option B: Normalize on write in both systems for exact cosine parity. This is simplest for consistent scoring.

Reranker recommendation (1k candidates):
- For 1k candidates, we typically do a two-stage approach:
  1) dense retrieval (vector similarity) to get ~1k candidates (fast).
  2) lightweight neural reranker (distil-bert or a small cross-encoder) to rescore top 100-200 if latency allows.
- Latency targets: Top-100 rerank with a distil-cross encoder typically adds ~80-150ms per request on a dedicated instance; we can push to <100ms with quantized weights.

SDK setup & auth:
- SDK init (python example):
  from redwood import RedwoodClient
  client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", region="us-west-2")

- We issue scoped API keys for ingestion only (no console access). For automation you can use a service-account style key with restricted scopes. We'll provide a short-lived onboarding key for the workshop.

Batching/backfill guidance:
- Backfill script pattern (pseudo):
  - chunk_size = 512
  - for chunk in chunked(csv_reader, chunk_size):
      client.embeddings.ingest(batch=chunk, normalize=True)

- For dual-write: add a write to Redwood in parallel with your existing write path, then verify parity on a 1% sample before full cutover.

Migration risk notes:
- Watch out for tokenization/model drift if you switch embedding model families. Keeping the same embedding model dims is the lowest-risk path.
- We'll provide an evaluation harness (sample queries + nDCG) to compare relevance pre/post.

I'll attach a small backfill script and a normalization snippet (dual-write-backfill-script.sh). Marcus sign-off.
